verses.text: On that day Deborah and Barak son of Abinoam sang this song:
"When the leaders in Israel lead the way, and the people gladly offer themselves, praise the LORD!
Listen, you kings! Pay attention, you rulers! I will sing to the LORD. I will sing praise to the LORD, the God of Israel.
LORD, when you went out from Seir, when you marched from the land of Edom, the earth shook, the skies poured, and the clouds poured down water.
The mountains shook before the LORD, the One of Sinai, before the LORD, the God of Israel.
In the days of Shamgar son of Anath, in the days of Jael, the main roads were empty. Travellers went along winding side paths.
Village life stopped in Israel. It stopped until I, Deborah, came, until I came as a mother in Israel.
When they chose new gods, war came to the city gates. Not a shield or spear was seen among forty thousand in Israel.
My heart is with Israel's leaders, who gladly offered themselves among the people. Praise the LORD!
You who ride on white donkeys, sitting on fine blankets, and you who walk along the road, think about this!
Away from the noise of the archers, at the watering places, they tell of the LORD's victories, the victories of his villagers in Israel. Then the LORD's people went down to the city gates.
Wake up, wake up, Deborah! Wake up, wake up, and sing a song! Get up, Barak! Lead away your prisoners, son of Abinoam!
Then the few who were left came down to the nobles. The LORD's people came down to me against the mighty.
Some came from Ephraim, whose roots were in Amalek. Benjamin came with your people after you. From Makir came leaders, and from Zebulun those who carry a commander's staff.
The princes of Issachar were with Deborah. Issachar was with Barak, rushing after him into the valley. Among the clans of Reuben there was much thinking and searching of heart.
Why did you stay among the sheep pens, listening to the shepherds whistling for the flocks? Among the clans of Reuben there was much searching of heart.
Gilead stayed east of the Jordan. And Dan, why did you stay by the ships? Asher stayed on the coast and remained in its harbours.
But the people of Zebulun risked their lives, and so did Naphtali on the high fields.
Kings came and fought. The kings of Canaan fought at Taanach, by the waters of Megiddo. But they took away no silver.
From the heavens the stars fought. From their paths in the sky they fought against Sisera.
The Kishon River swept them away, the ancient river, the Kishon River. March on, my soul, be strong!
Then the horses' hooves thundered as his mighty horses galloped and galloped.
'Curse Meroz,' said the angel of the LORD. 'Bitterly curse its people, because they did not come to help the LORD, to help the LORD against the mighty.'
Most blessed of women is Jael, the wife of Heber the Kenite. She is most blessed of women who live in tents.
He asked for water, and she gave him milk. In a fine bowl she brought him cream.
She reached for the tent peg with her hand, and for the worker's hammer with her right hand. She struck Sisera and crushed his head. She smashed and pierced the side of his head.
At her feet he sank down. He fell and lay there. At her feet he sank and fell. Where he sank, there he fell, dead.
Sisera's mother looked out through the window. Behind the lattice she cried out, 'Why is his chariot taking so long to come? Why are the hoofbeats of his chariots so slow?'
The wisest of her ladies answered her, and she kept telling herself,

'They must be finding and sharing out the goods they took: a girl or two for each man, colourful clothes as plunder for Sisera, colourful embroidered clothes, two pieces of embroidered cloth for my neck, all taken as plunder.'
So may all your enemies die, LORD! But may all who love you be like the sun when it rises in its strength." Then the land had peace for forty years.
